source.title: World Bank, World Development Indicators: households and NPISHs final consumption expenditure (NE.CON.PRVT.CD) ÷ population (SP.POP.TOTL), 2024

rows.explainer: What an average person in the United Kingdom consumes in a year, in US dollars at the market rate (a pound amount × @fx.usd_per_gbp_<year> is on the same footing): the base a UK model's ln(consumption) gain is measured against, scaled to its recipients by the model's own share of the mean.

rows.label: Consumption per person of refugees in their first year and people seeking asylum in the UK, as a share of the UK survey average

source.title: GOV.UK, Asylum support: what you'll get
source.quote: You'll usually get £49.18 for each person in your household.

rows.explainer: People seeking asylum live on £49.18 a week (about £2,560 a year) in self-catered housing, or £9.95 a week in hotels with meals provided, with the accommodation provided by the Home Office; with the housing and meals at their value, a few thousand pounds a year, under a fifth of the UK survey average (@united_kingdom.consumption_per_person_2024 × @survey_consumption.survey_to_na_gbr, about $27,000). Newly recognised and resettled refugees in their first year live on Universal Credit (£393 a month for a single adult over 25 in 2024/25) with council-arranged or temporary housing, a little more. 18%, range 10% to 30%. Read by every model of help to refugees and people seeking asylum in the UK, so they value the same people the same way.
